anomaly_def.Name: Query Plan Selection Anomaly + Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Query Plan Selection Anomaly : The optimizer reuses or chooses a markedly sub-optimal execution plan even though statistics are reasonably accurate.
Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly : Concurrent sessions serialize on hot buffer pages, page latches, or related lightweight locks, stalling on buffer-manager structures rather than row-level locks.

When both root causes are active, the database experiences a feedback loop in which a poor plan amplifies latch pressure and the resulting contention magnifies the performance penalty of the bad plan. Observable symptoms include: 
• Sudden plan switches from index seeks to full scans that explode logical and physical I/O, immediately followed by spikes in BUF_BUSY/PAGE_LATCH wait events. 
• High CPU spin time with little throughput while multiple sessions run the same cached but sub-optimal plan. 
• Hot-spot pages such as index roots, sequence blocks, or a narrow range of heap pages becoming latch bottlenecks because the inefficient plan drives excessive, repetitive accesses. 
• Wide variance in query latency; some executions hang on latch waits while others recompile and obtain yet another unstable plan, making performance diagnosis confusing.

Causal chain: A flawed plan can dramatically increase the number of page touches (e.g., table scans or nested loops with large outer row counts). This floods the buffer pool, concentrates access on a small set of pages, and lengthens dirty-page residency, all of which raise latch acquisition times. The heightened contention slows query completion, keeping the bad plan active longer and increasing concurrency on the same hot pages, further reinforcing the contention. In turn, the elongated execution times and fluctuating runtime statistics may trigger opportunistic recompilations that choose different but still sub-optimal plans, perpetuating the cycle and degrading overall system stability.

entry.official_description: Error while loading time zone description from mysql.time_zone_transition table: bad transition type id
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with a general engine-level execution problem surfaced by the official error catalogue, but its precise trigger must be interpreted together with workload context and surrounding evidence.
entry.solution_guidance: Review the surrounding workload, official description, and engine state to determine whether the issue is rooted in SQL logic, resource pressure, configuration, or environmental instability.
